highlights.description: A Go-first, machine-readable description of a product's pricing and packaging: tiers, plans with prices, features (switches and ordered levels), limits (with periods and fair use), one-time products, a marketplace fee, and the application access each tier grants
Safe by construction: an unknown plan is the default plan, an unset feature is off, an unset limit is zero, and unlimited is its own field
Validation with stable error codes (E001 to E013) that reports every error at once, and lint warnings (W001 to W006) for review
Projections computed from the spec: a pricing view, a tier-to-entitlement map, and a diff that marks what affects existing customers

added.description: `pricingspec` types: `Spec`, `Tier`, `Feature`, `Limit`, `Plan`, `Price`, `FeatureValue`, `LimitValue`, `Product`, `Marketplace` and `TierGrant`, following the static-type profile with no schema composition
`schema/pricing.schema.json` generated from the Go types and embedded, with a test that fails when it is out of date
`Load` and `Parse` decode strictly, reject unknown fields and unknown format versions, and return a `*ValidationError` listing every error rule broken (E001 to E013) with a path

`Spec.Lint` reports the review warnings W001 to W006: unlimited defaults without fair use, a higher tier priced under a lower one, unused features and limits, tiers without grants, level names that read as options, and annual prices that are no saving
Helpers `PlanOrDefault`, `Has`, `Level`, `AtLeast`, `Allowance`, `Check` (allowed, warn or refuse), `GrantsFor` and `TierRank`; an unknown identifier never grants more
`PricingView` orders plans by tier and lines features and limits up across them as data for a page; `EntitlementMap` lists each tier's grants in rank order

`Diff` compares two specs in a stable order and marks price increases, lowered allowances, removed features, lowered levels, removed grants, higher fees and removed plans as affecting existing customers
Examples of a subscription tool and a marketplace, both invented, kept valid and free of warnings by tests

documentation.description: `SPEC.md` is the normative description of the model, the rule codes, resolution, projections and the mapping from a tier to account entitlements
The fit of the model to three product shapes is recorded, with the changes it required
A user guide covers concepts, writing a spec and using a spec, built as an MkDocs site

tests.description: A test for every error and warning code, the loader's rejections, the helpers, golden files for the projections and the diff, and schema validation of the examples

infrastructure.description: Module, license, lint configuration and CI workflows
